d: Nostr Vault docs: getting started on iPhone, Android, Mac and the web, your keys and signers, the mesh, My Devices and kiosk mode.
x: Start here iPhone and iPad TestFlight, iOS 17+ Android Zapstore or APK, Android 8+ Mac Menu bar app, macOS 14+ Web browser Nothing to install Can't find it? Search the docs with the box at the top of the menu. If the answer isn't here, ask on Nostr or open an issue on GitHub .

d: Install Nostr Vault on an iPhone or iPad, create a Nostr account or bring the one you have, and find your way around.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Find your way around · Next
x: Nostr Vault runs your own Nostr relay on your phone. Your posts, messages and media are kept on the phone, and copies go out to public relays so people can see them. Install Nostr Vault needs iOS 17 or later, on an iPhone or an iPad. Join the beta on TestFlight , install it, and open it. Pick a way in The first screen has two buttons. What's inside? under them lists what the app does. Create an account if you're new to Nostr. You get a new key, a password for it and a profile. I already use Nostr if you have an account from another Nostr app. You bring that account, and your old notes come home to your phone. Create an account Welcome to Nostr. A short explanation of Nostr and your vault. Tap Create My Account . Your Keys. Two keys replace a username and password. The public key is your name on Nostr; share it freely. The secret key is your password; anyone who has it can post as you. Tap Copy next to the secret key and save it in your password manager. Nobody can recover it for you. Tick I saved my secret key , then Continue . Protect Your Key. Choose a password of at least 8 characters. It locks your secret key on this phone. Nobody can reset it, so write it down too. Your Profile. Add a photo and a name, or tap Skip for Now . You can change both later. Welcome to Nostr! Your account is made and your relay is running. Tap Start Exploring . Fill your feed. Nostr starts empty: no algorithm picks for you. Tap Let's fill it , pick a few topics, and follow people whose posts you like. Five follows build your web of trust, which fills your feed and filters out spam. Not now skips it. You're done when your Following feed shows posts from the people you followed. Bring the account you have Tap I already use Nostr . The screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste one of these into the box, or tap Scan your key or signer link to scan a QR code. The app tells you what you'll be able to do: You paste The app shows What you get Your npub, or name@domain Read-only Your feed, notes and follows. Add your secret key later in Settings to post. Your nsec (secret key) You can post Post, reply, DM and zap. You choose a password, and the key is saved encrypted on this phone. It's never sent anywhere. An ncryptsec (a key locked with a password) Encrypted key · you can post Enter the password you locked it with. A bunker:// link from a signer app Signer link · you can post Your signer app approves each post. Your key never touches Nostr Vault. To use a signer app instead, tap Use a signer app , then Sign in with Clave . See Signers . Checking your relays. The app looks for your notes on your relays. Tap Start import . Bringing your notes home. A few cards explain what's happening while your notes are copied to your phone. A long history takes a while. Wait, or tap Keep it running in the background and start using the app; the import carries on. Pasting a secret key into any app is a risk. A signer keeps the key out of Nostr Vault altogether. If you do paste it, Nostr Vault keeps it encrypted on this phone only. Find your way around The tab bar along the bottom: Feed : posts from the people you follow. Hold the tab and slide up to switch feeds: Following, Discover, Global, Media, Articles and more. Search : people, posts and hashtags. Profile , in the middle: your profile. The gear at the top opens Settings . WoT : your web of trust, the people you follow and the people they follow, on a globe. Vault : everything your relay keeps on this phone, and your messages. On iPad the same places are in the sidebar, Settings included. Some pages show a short tour the first time you open them. Replay any of them from Settings → Help → Tutorials . Next Your keys and accounts : add another account, back up your key, switch signers. The mesh : connect your phone to your Mac and your other devices (3.0).

d: Install Nostr Vault on an Android phone, choose where your notes live, create a Nostr account or bring yours with Amber or another signer.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Where should your notes live? · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Just look around · Find your way around · Next
x: Nostr Vault runs your own Nostr relay inside the app. Your posts, messages and media are kept on your phone, and copies go out to public relays so people can see them. Install Nostr Vault needs Android 8.0 or later. Get it from Zapstore , or download the APK from the latest release on GitHub and open it. Android asks you to allow installs from that app the first time. Pick a way in The first screen has three buttons. What's inside? under them lists what the app does. Create an account if you're new to Nostr. I already use Nostr if you have an account from another Nostr app. Your old notes come home to your phone. Just look around to read with your public key only. You can't post until you add a key or a signer. Where should your notes live? Every way in asks this first. Built-in Relay (recommended): your own relay and media server, inside the app. Pick this unless you know you want the other one. A Relay You Already Run : a relay app on this phone, such as Citrine, or your own relay elsewhere, such as Nostr Vault on your Mac. Fill in Relay URL , and Blossom URL (optional) for media. The built-in relay never starts, and setup skips importing your notes. You can change it later in Settings → Advanced . Create an account Welcome to Nostr. Tap Create My Account . Your Keys. The public key is your name on Nostr; share it freely. The secret key is your password; anyone who has it can post as you. Copy it into your password manager. Nobody can recover it for you. Tick I saved my secret key , then Continue . Protect Your Key. Choose a password of at least 8 characters. It locks your secret key on this phone, and nobody can reset it. Your Profile. Add a photo and a name, or tap Skip for Now . Welcome to Nostr! Tap Start Exploring , then follow the short guide that helps you find people. Five follows build your web of trust, which fills your feed and filters out spam. Bring the account you have Tap I already use Nostr , choose where your notes live, and the screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste your npub or name@domain ( Read-only ), your nsec ( You can post , and you choose a password), an ncryptsec ( Encrypted key · you can post ), or a bunker:// link ( Signer link · you can post ). Scan your key or signer link reads a QR code. Or use a signer, so your secret key never enters Nostr Vault: Use Amber shows when Amber is installed on this phone. Use a signer app then Sign in with a signer app opens Amber or another signer on this phone, or shows a code to scan with a signer on another device. See Signers . Checking your relays. Tap Start import . Bringing your notes home. Wait for the import, or tap Keep it running in the background and start using the app. Just look around Choose where your notes live. Enter your identity. Type your npub or name@domain, or scan a QR code, and tap Resolve & Continue . Import Notes. Import from Network copies your notes from public relays to your phone. Restore from Backup reads a Nostr Vault backup file (.zip). Or skip. Ready to Browse. Tap Launch Nostr Vault . To post later, add your key or a signer in Accounts & Keys . Find your way around The tab bar along the bottom has Feed , Search , Profile in the middle, WoT (your web of trust) and Vault (everything your relay keeps, and your messages). The gear on your Profile opens Settings . Replay the app's short tours from Settings → Help → Tutorials . Next Your keys and accounts The mesh : connect your phone to your Mac and your other devices (3.0).

d: Install Nostr Vault on a Mac, set it up from the menu bar, and keep your relay running while the app is open.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Just look around · Find your way around · Next
x: On a Mac, Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar and runs your own Nostr relay while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac becomes the always-on home for your notes and media. Install Nostr Vault needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Download it from the latest release on GitHub (the NostrVault-macOS-….zip file), unzip it, and drag Nostr Vault into Applications. The first time it opens, a Welcome to Nostr Vault window says Nostr Vault lives in your menu bar . Click Get Started . Setup opens next. Pick a way in Create an account if you're new to Nostr. I already use Nostr to bring your account, your notes and your media. Just look around to read with your public key only. Create an account The same steps as on the iPhone: Create My Account , save your secret key on Your Keys and tick I saved my secret key , choose a password on Protect Your Key , then a photo and name on Your Profile (or Skip for Now ), and Start Exploring . The details are on Get started on iPhone . Bring the account you have Enter Your Keys. Pick how you sign: Private Key : paste your nsec and choose a password. The key is encrypted on this Mac. Remote Signer : Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan with Clave. Or paste a bunker link from any signer app. Your key stays in the signer. No account yet? New to Nostr? Generate Keys makes one here. Your Personal Relay. Your relay runs on this Mac either way. A Relay Domain (optional) makes it reachable from your other devices. Leave it blank for local only, or tap Skip — configure later . Bring Your Notes Home. From Network copies your notes from public relays to this Mac; From Backup restores a Nostr Vault backup. Tap Import Notes , or Skip — I'll start fresh . Mirror Your Media. Copies your photos and videos from a Blossom media server, or from a backup, to this Mac. Tap Sync Media or Skip Media . Lightning (NWC). Paste a Nostr Wallet Connect link to send zaps, or Skip — set up later . You're All Set. Click Launch Nostr Vault . Just look around Enter Your Public Key (your npub or name@domain), import your notes if you like, and Ready to Browse opens the app. Re-run setup later to post, DM and zap. Find your way around Click the Nostr Vault icon in the menu bar. The panel shows your relay's status, your notes and your media. Open Window opens the full window, with the feed. The gear ( Settings (⌘,) ) opens Settings. Your relay runs while Nostr Vault is open. Quit Nostr Vault stops it. To keep it running, open Settings → Startup and turn on Launch at Login and Start Relay Automatically . Next The mesh : make your Mac the photo server and vault for your phones (3.0). Your keys and accounts

t: Use Nostr Vault in a browser
d: Open the Nostr Vault web app at nostrvault.app/vault/, sign in with a browser extension, a bunker link or read-only, and know what the web app keeps in your browser.
h: Sign in · Opening a shared post · Find your way around · Your data in this browser · Next
x: The web app is Nostr Vault in a browser tab, with nothing to install. It's in beta. Open nostrvault.app/vault/ in any up-to-date browser, on a computer or a phone. Like the apps, it runs your own relay, here inside the browser. Your notes and messages are kept in this browser's storage. Sign in The web app never asks for your secret key. Sign in with something that holds the key for you: A browser extension. If a Nostr signing extension is installed in this browser, Sign in with extension shows. Click it and approve in the extension. A remote signer. Paste a bunker:// link from your signer app into Bunker link (NIP-46) , click Connect bunker , and approve the connection in your signer. See Signers . Read-only. Type your name, npub or name@domain and click Find me . You can read your feed but not post. Accounts you've used in this browser are listed at the top next time, so one click signs you back in. Opening a shared post A post shared from Nostr Vault opens in the web app, and anyone can read it without signing in. The top says Viewing as a guest . Click Sign in there to reply, like or zap. A guest's browser keeps nothing once the tab is closed. Find your way around The same places as the phone apps: Feed , Search , Profile , WoT and Vault . On a phone they're a tab bar at the bottom; in a wide window they're a sidebar, and a post opens next to the list. Settings is the gear on your profile. Your data in this browser Settings → Backup & Restore → Download backup saves every event you signed that this browser holds, one per line (.jsonl). Messages and what others sent you aren't in it. Restore puts a backup file back into this browser. Only events signed by you are taken, and nothing is published. Under This browser's copy , Sign out and delete this browser's copy removes everything this browser holds. Your phone's vault is untouched. Clearing your browser's site data deletes the web app's copy too. Your posts are still on public relays and in your phone or Mac vault. Next Signers : which signer to use on which device. For your own always-on vault, get the app for iPhone , Android or Mac .

d: What your Nostr keys are, where Nostr Vault keeps them, and how to add accounts, switch between them, back up your secret key and remove a key.
h: Two keys · Where to find them · Add another account · Switch accounts · Back up your secret key · Change how an account signs · Remove a key or an account · Publish Relay List · Next
x: A Nostr account is a pair of keys. Nostr Vault keeps them on your device, or leaves the secret one with a signer app, and never on a server. Two keys Public key (starts with npub ): your name on Nostr. Share it freely. With only this, an app can show your feed but can't post as you. Secret key (starts with nsec ): your password to Nostr. Anyone who has it can post as you, forever. Nobody can reset it or recover it for you, not even us. Nostr Vault can sign for you in two ways: A local key. Your secret key, locked with a password you choose (at least 8 characters), and kept on this device only. A key locked this way starts with ncryptsec . A signer. A separate app holds your secret key and approves each post. Nostr Vault never sees the key. See Signers . Where to find them Device Open iPhone, iPad, Android Profile tab → gear → Accounts & Keys Mac Menu bar icon → gear → Accounts & Keys Web Settings → Accounts & Keys Each account shows how it signs: Local Key , Remote Signer , Amber (Android), or no signing key at all (read-only). The first account you set up is the Owner : it's the one your vault relay belongs to. Add another account In Accounts & Keys , tap Add Account . Paste the account's key. iPhone, iPad and Mac take its npub. Then open the new account and tap Import Private Key or Connect Remote Signer to post with it. Android takes an npub, an nsec or an ncryptsec, or Connect Remote Signer (NIP-46) . Web signs in with the account's own extension or bunker. The account you're using stays signed in. Switch accounts iPhone: hold your picture in the middle of the tab bar and pick an account. It only opens when you have more than one. Mac: the account button in the menu bar panel. Everywhere: open the account in Accounts & Keys and tap Switch to This Account . A post is always sent from the account that was active when you tapped Post. Back up your secret key Do this once, right after you make an account, and keep the key in a password manager. Open the account in Accounts & Keys . Tap Reveal Key (Android: Reveal Private Key ). The app checks it's you with Face ID, Touch ID or your device passcode, then asks for the key's password. Copy the key into your password manager. Don't paste it into a chat, a note or a screenshot. With a signer, there's no key to reveal here. Back it up in the signer app. Change how an account signs Import Private Key adds a local key to an account that only had a public key or a signer. Tick Encrypt with Password to lock it. Connect Remote Signer adds a signer. It must hold this account's key; a signer for another account is refused. With both, Sign With (Android: Signing ) picks which one signs. Remove a key or an account Remove Local Key deletes the secret key from this device. If it's your only copy, it's gone for good. Disconnect Remote Signer drops the signer's connection. Reconnecting needs a fresh bunker link. Remove Account takes the account, and any key or signer for it, off this device. Nothing on the relays changes, but you need the key again to sign back in. Publish Relay List Publish Relay List tells other Nostr apps which relays you read from and write to, so they can find your posts and reach you. Your own relay is always included. Next Signers : Amber, Clave, bunker links and browser extensions.

d: Keep your Nostr secret key out of Nostr Vault with a signer: Amber on Android, Clave on iPhone, a bunker link from any signer app, or a browser extension on the web.
h: Which signer, where · Sign in with a signer during setup · Add a signer to an account you already have · On the web · Good to know
x: A signer is a separate app that holds your secret key. When Nostr Vault wants to post, like or send a message as you, it asks the signer, and the signer approves. Your key never enters Nostr Vault, so a problem in Nostr Vault can't leak it. Which signer, where Device Signers How it connects Android Amber, or any signer app on the phone Use Amber , or Use a signer app → Sign in with a signer app iPhone and iPad Clave Use a signer app → Sign in with Clave Mac Clave on your iPhone Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan Web A Nostr browser extension Sign in with extension Everywhere Any signer that gives a bunker link (NIP-46), such as nsec.app or your own bunker Paste or scan the bunker:// link Sign in with a signer during setup Choose I already use Nostr . On iPhone and Android, the next screen has Use a signer app under the box (and Use Amber on Android when Amber is installed). On a Mac, choose Remote Signer . The signer opens, or a code shows on screen to scan with a signer on another device. Approve the connection in the signer, then come back to Nostr Vault. If the signer didn't open, tap Open Clave again (Android: Open signer again ), or Copy link and open it yourself. Or paste a bunker:// link from any signer app into the same box. Add a signer to an account you already have Open Settings → Accounts & Keys and tap the account. Tap Connect Remote Signer . Paste the bunker link into Bunker URI , or scan its QR code. On iPhone you can Sign in with Clave here too. Approve the connection in your signer app. The signer has to hold this account's key. A signer for a different account is refused. On the web The web app only signs with a signer: a browser extension, or a bunker link in Bunker link (NIP-46) and Connect bunker . It never asks for your secret key. A bunker's connection to the browser is stored encrypted, and removing the account or signing out asks the bunker to drop it. Good to know Posts, likes and messages are signed by the signer, which may ask you to approve each one. If nothing happens, open the signer and check for a pending request. To stop using a signer, open the account and tap Disconnect Remote Signer . Revoke the connection in the signer app too. Back up your secret key in the signer app. Nostr Vault can't show it to you, because it never has it.

d: How the Nostr Vault wallet works: connect a Lightning wallet with a Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) link, turn on zap buttons, disconnect, and the on-chain Bitcoin address under Advanced.
h: What the wallet is · Connect a wallet · Turning on zap buttons · Saving the wallet to your Nostr account · Disconnecting · Bitcoin On-Chain · The Wallet Connect tutorial
x: The basics What the wallet is A zap is a small bitcoin tip sent over Lightning (bitcoin's fast payment network) to the person who posted. Amounts are in sats , the smallest unit of bitcoin. Nostr Vault never holds that money. Your sats stay in a Lightning wallet you run somewhere else, such as Alby Hub, Coinos, Primal or Zeus. Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) is a standard way for an app to ask that wallet to pay. Your wallet gives you a link that starts with nostr+walletconnect:// , and you paste it into Nostr Vault. Treat the link like cash. Anyone who has it can spend from that wallet. If your wallet lets you, make a connection with a spending limit just for Nostr Vault. Step by step Connect a wallet In your wallet app, find Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) and copy the connection link. In Nostr Vault, open Settings → Account → Wallet . Paste the link into the Wallet Connect box (on Android it's called Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) ). On the web, tap Connect wallet . The app pastes the link only. There is no QR scanner for it. Once a wallet is connected you'll see its Balance and can set your Default Zap (on Android, Default Zap Amount (sats) ), the amount one tap sends. On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android you can also start from your own profile. Tap the bolt, labelled Lightning . With no wallet yet, it shows No Wallet Connected and a Connect a wallet button that takes you to the same place. On Android the wallet is on the Settings tab of that screen. Once connected, the Lightning screen shows your balance and lets you receive with an invoice, pay an invoice, lightning address or LNURL, and see your history if your wallet shares it. Opt in Turning on zap buttons Zap buttons on posts are a choice you make under Settings → Appearance → Post buttons . Add ⚡️ in the Add ⚡️ field to show a zap button, and remove it to hide the button. Zapping someone from their profile is always available. iPhone, iPad and Mac: the zap button is off until you add ⚡️. It then shows on posts, live streams and locked articles. Android: ⚡️ is there by default, so posts show a zap button until you remove it. Web: notes show a zap button. A tap sends your default zap, and holding it lets you pick another amount. Each zap goes straight from your wallet to the author. Nostr Vault takes no cut. Phones and Mac Saving the wallet to your Nostr account On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android, the Wallet page can switch on Save wallet to my Nostr account . The link is then stored encrypted to your key on your relays, so Nostr Vault on your other devices (or the Wisp app) can pick it up with Use saved wallet . Anyone who has your Nostr key can read it and spend from the wallet. Remove from my account takes it off again. Stop using it Disconnecting iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android: delete the link from the Wallet Connect box. If you saved it to your account, also tap Remove from my account . Web: tap Disconnect wallet , then Disconnect . The web app keeps the link only in that browser, and deletes it when you sign out. To be sure the app can't spend any more, also revoke the connection in your wallet app. Advanced Bitcoin On-Chain Separate from Lightning, the apps can make a regular bitcoin address from your Nostr key. It lives under Settings → Advanced → Bitcoin On-Chain on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android. It isn't in the web app. Turn on Bitcoin Address to see the address and a QR code, and use Copy Address to share it. Sweep Wallet sends everything at that address to another address you choose. This one is different. Bitcoin sent to this address is controlled by your Nostr key, so anyone with your key can spend it. Before a sweep, the app warns you not to send to a hardware wallet or an exchange: that would tie your npub to that wallet on the public blockchain, and it can't be undone. Learn in the app The Wallet Connect tutorial On iPhone, iPad and Android, Settings → Help → Tutorials has a short Wallet Connect tour. It points at the e

d: How Nostr Vault's mesh works: your phone or Mac serves your own photos over the FIPS mesh, with no public IP, domain or cloud. My Devices, kiosk mode, share pages and privacy.
h: What the mesh is · Your phone or Mac as your photo server · My Devices · Kiosk mode · Share pages · Privacy · What's live vs what's in 3.0
x: The basics What the mesh is Most phones and home computers can't be reached from the internet. They sit behind a home router, move between Wi-Fi and cell, and have no fixed address. That's why your photos normally live on someone else's server. FIPS is a mesh network where you reach a device by its Nostr key (an npub) instead of an IP address. It works across home routers and mobile networks, and the connection between two devices is encrypted end to end. Nostr Vault uses it to let your devices reach each other, and to let other people fetch your photos from you. Photos stay trustworthy no matter who hands them over. On Nostr, a photo is named by its fingerprint (a hash). Whoever sends it, the app checks the fingerprint, and if it matches, it's the photo. If it doesn't, the photo is thrown away and loaded the normal way. Your own server Your phone or Mac as your photo server Your Nostr profile already keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault adds one more entry to that list: your own device, written as its mesh address. It goes after your normal media servers, so apps that don't know about the mesh carry on as before. An app that does know about it can ask your device for a photo directly, by its fingerprint, the same way it would ask any media server. Your photos still go to your normal servers too. Your device is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. On a Mac , the Nostr Vault app serves while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac is an always-on photo server. On a phone , it serves while the app is open, or full-time in kiosk mode on a spare phone. To turn it on, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh and switch on Mesh . Serving is off until you turn it on. Your devices, together My Devices My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, home vault and browser page that reach each other over the mesh. Devices on this list sync with each other in full: your notes, your photos and your history. On each device, open Settings → Mesh → FIPS Mesh , turn on Mesh , and in This Device tap Copy . That's the device's mesh address. On your other devices, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste it, and pick what it is: Vault on Mac , Phone or Home vault . Do it in both directions: add each phone on the Mac, and the Mac on each phone. A device on the list shows a dot when it's in reach. To check that everything arrived, use FIPS Mesh → Sync → Check sync on a phone. An always-on vault Kiosk mode Kiosk mode turns a phone into a small always-on vault. Put an old phone on a charger at home, turn kiosk mode on under Share With Others , and it keeps serving. It keeps the screen on, so the phone keeps serving. Leaving the app pauses kiosk mode, and it turns on again when you come back. Your own devices in My Devices reach it in full. Everyone else can only read the photos in your posts, and only slowly: 1 MB/s shared between all of them, at most 256 MB each, and 1 GB per session before they have to wait. They can't read your notes or change anything. You can also limit who can view to only your own devices. Set another phone to use it as its Home vault , and your new notes and photos go to the kiosk phone over the mesh, which sends your notes on to your relays. Works in any browser Share pages When you share a post from Nostr Vault, the link opens that post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. Anyone can read it as a guest, with no account and nothing to install, and sign in from there to reply or like. If a photo in that post or its replies can't be loaded from its usual server, the browser fetches it from that author's own device over the mesh. It joins the mesh for that one visit with a throwaway key, asks the device for the photo by its fingerprint, checks the fingerprint, and shows it. The photo is fetched by the visitor's own browser. nostrvault.app keeps no copy of it, and a guest's browser keeps nothing once the tab is closed. You may see blob:https://nostrvault.app/ as the image addr

d: The Nostr Vault browser relay at nostrvault.app/relay/: a browser tab that keeps your notes and serves them to your own devices over the FIPS mesh. Pairing, Start FIPS, the screensaver, My Devices and limits.
h: What the browser relay is · Pair your iPhone with the page · What it keeps and serves · The screensaver · When the tab closes · In My Devices · Limits and privacy
x: The basics What the browser relay is A relay is a server that stores Nostr notes and hands them out. The browser relay is one that runs inside a web page, at nostrvault.app/relay/ . It stores notes in the browser's own storage on that device and joins the FIPS mesh, so your own devices can reach it by its key. New to the mesh? Read The mesh first. The page keeps no Nostr key of yours. Your notes arrive already signed, and the page checks each signature. A good spot for it is an old phone or tablet on a charger. Set it up Pair your iPhone with the page On your iPhone, open FIPS Mesh and turn the mesh on. Under This Device , tap Copy . That's the phone's mesh address. On the device that will run the page, open nostrvault.app/relay/ . Paste the address into the box under the FIPS heading (one address per line) and tap Save owners . The page reloads. Tap Start FIPS . The status shows the page's own mesh address . Copy it. On the iPhone, go to My Devices → Add a device by address , paste the page's address, and pick Browser page . The phone then connects for the page. If it doesn't, open the page's entry in My Devices and tap Connect this phone . Copy this phone's mesh address is there too. A link of the form nostrvault.app/relay/#owner=npub1 also adds an owner. The page asks you to confirm each address first, because an owner can write to the page and read everything on it. Only accept your own. What it does What it keeps and serves Your new notes. While the iPhone app is open, each new note you post also goes to the page. Send my latest notes sends your 20 most recent notes from the phone. The result line says how many the page kept. In this testing build, check that number: if it says 0 kept, the page did not take your notes. Checked notes only. The page checks each note's signature and turns away notes from authors it isn't set up for. Owners only. The page serves notes on the mesh only to the addresses saved as owners. Anyone else's connection is dropped without an answer. Photos, read only. Under Show photo , you can paste a photo's fingerprint (sha256) or a .fips link and the page fetches it from a paired vault. It shows the photo only if the fingerprint matches. Photos aren't stored on the page. The page reaches your phone through the public mesh entry points (seeds). Once both ends are connected it tries a direct link. On the iPhone, leave the middle server under Advanced on its public setting. With None , a browser page only connects on the same network. Keep it awake The screensaver Start screensaver fills the screen with a black "relay running" view: a count, the uptime, whether the screen is kept awake (the wake lock), and whether the seed is up. Tap anywhere to leave it. After a reload, start it again. The count on this screen is the page's own test notes, not your notes. Report shows storage, uptime gaps and a signature self-test, if you want the details. When it stops When the tab closes The relay only runs while the page is open and the screen is on. Closed, locked or in the background, nothing reaches it. Notes the phone sends while the page is down are not queued. Tap Send my latest notes once it's back. Stored notes stay in the browser and are there when you reopen the page. Tap Start FIPS again; it doesn't start by itself. Stop FIPS takes the page off the mesh. The page's mesh key lives in the browser's site data. Clear that data and the page gets a new address, so pair it again. Your devices list In My Devices The page shows up in My Devices as a Browser page , the role whose job reads "Gets your new notes while this app is open." You can have one browser page per account; adding a new one replaces the old. To stop sending, open its entry and tap Remove from my devices . Anything already on the page stays there. Android and Mac also offer Browser page under My Devices → Add a device by address . In this build, only the iPhone app sends notes to the page. Be candid Limits and privacy The tab must stay open. d: What the Nostr Vault vault relay keeps on your phone or Mac: your notes, mentions, messages and media. The Vault tab, starting and stopping it, Import Notes, and the Mac and web differences.
h: What your vault is · The Vault tab · Vault settings · Import your past notes · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What your vault is Most Nostr apps only read and write to other people's relays. Nostr Vault also runs one on your device. Your vault is a personal Nostr relay and a Blossom media server, and it keeps a copy of: Your own notes , everything you post, like, zap and save. Notes that mention you , from people you trust (see Who Can Reach You ). Your direct messages , still encrypted. Recent notes from people you follow , so your feed loads fast. Older ones are cleared out over time. Your media , in its Blossom media server. The vault's address ( ws://127.0.0.1: ) only works on that device, so nobody else can connect to it. Your notes still go to your normal relays too. The vault is the copy you own. To see it explained in the app, open Settings → Help → Tutorials and play Vault in Your Pocket or How Your Vault Works . iPhone and Android The Vault tab The Vault tab shows how your vault is doing. At the top it says Your vault is running , starting, paused or needs a restart, with how long it's been up. If it stops, a button lets you start it again so it catches up on new notes and messages. The menu on that card has Copy Address , Restart , Stop and Start . Below that: Who can reach you : how many people can send to your inbox. In your vault : how many events it holds and how much space notes, media and cache use. The cache is other people's media kept for quick loading, and you can clear it. Keep it full : Import notes , import media, back up media and export notes. Vault settings : shortcuts to Relays, Who Can Reach You, Media Servers and starting automatically. On Android the same screen is called Vault Dashboard . Settings Vault settings Everything about the vault is grouped under Settings → Your Vault Relay . The card at the top of Settings shows whether it's running, with a Start Relay button if it isn't. Start Relay Automatically : start the vault when the app opens. Leave it on. Sync with Vault on Mac : send your notes and photos to Nostr Vault on your Mac (3.0, see The mesh ). Who Can Reach You : who may send to your inbox and messages. More . Import Notes : fill the vault with your past notes. See below. Backup & Restore : save or restore your vault as a file. More . Bring your history Import your past notes A new vault starts empty. Import Notes pulls your old notes, and notes where you are tagged, from your other relays into the vault, starting at a date you pick. Open Settings → Your Vault Relay → Import Notes and set the Start Date . On iPhone, run it from the Vault tab: Keep it full → Import notes . On Android, tap Start Import on the same page. It reads from the relays that have Import switched on in Settings → Relays . Notes that tag you are kept only if they come from people you trust, or if they reply to or quote your own posts. Where it runs Phone, Mac and web Where the vault runs What's different iPhone Inside the app Vault tab with the full dashboard. Android Inside the app Same as iPhone; the dashboard is called Vault Dashboard. Mac Inside the menu bar app A simpler Relay Dashboard. Domain & Port lets you give the vault your own domain so your other devices can reach it, and Startup has Launch at Login . Web In your browser's storage No relay settings. Import with Import from my relays . Signing out deletes this browser's copy; your phone's vault is untouched. A vault on the web is a copy, not a backup. It lives in that browser. Use Sign out and delete this browser's copy on a shared computer, and keep real backups with Backup & Restore .

d: Nostr Vault's Who Can Reach You settings: Follow Distance, Minimum Followers and Refresh Trust List decide which people can send to your vault's inbox and messages. Spam control by Web of Trust.
h: What it controls · Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What it controls Your vault has an inbox, where notes that mention you land, and a chat store for your direct messages. Anyone on Nostr can try to send to them. Who Can Reach You keeps out everyone who isn't close to you in your follows. This is your Web of Trust, and it's the vault's spam filter. Mentions and messages from people outside your trust list are turned away. Replies and quotes of your own posts still get in, from anyone. Your messages can only be read by people on the list who sign in. Your own notes aren't affected. You can always post. Open it from Settings → Your Vault Relay → Who Can Reach You , or tap Who can reach you on the Vault tab, which shows how many people can reach your inbox right now. The settings Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List Follow Distance How many follows away someone can be and still reach you. Lower is more private. Distance Who can reach you 1 Only you. 2 You and the people you follow. 3 (default) You, the people you follow, and the people they follow, if enough of your follows follow them (see Minimum Followers). The control goes up to 5, but 4 and 5 work the same as 3. Minimum Followers At distance 3, how many of the people you follow must also follow someone before they can reach you. The default is 3. Raise it to keep out more strangers, lower it to let more friends of friends in. It has no effect at distance 1 or 2. Refresh Trust List How often the vault rebuilds the list from your follows: Every hour , Every 12 hours , Every day (default) or Every week . Someone you just followed can reach you after the next rebuild. Rate Limits Leave these as they are. Where to find it Phone, Mac and web iPhone and Mac have the same screen. On the Mac it's in the Settings sidebar. Android has the same settings, and restarts the vault for you when you change one. The web has no trust settings. Its Who Can Reach You row opens the browser relay's mesh panel, where Who can reach this relay is a list of your own vaults' mesh addresses. Not getting a mention you expected? The sender may be too far from you. Follow them, or raise Follow Distance, then wait for the next trust list refresh.

d: How to back up and restore Nostr Vault: export and import notes and media in Backup & Restore, restore an old follow list from Following Backup, un-delete posts in Recently Deleted, and the web backup.
h: Backup & Restore · Following Backup · Recently Deleted · Backups on the web
x: Notes and media Backup & Restore Open Settings → Your Vault Relay → Backup & Restore . It has two parts, and each one is its own file. Notes. Export Notes saves everything in your vault as a .zip: your notes, private notes, messages (still encrypted), the notes that mention you and your feed cache. Import Notes puts a notes backup back. Media. Export Media saves the photos and videos in your vault's media server as a .zip. Import Media puts them back. On iPhone the file goes to the share sheet, so you can save it to Files or send it to your Mac. On the Mac and Android you pick where to save it. A restore adds to what's already in the vault. Anything it already has is skipped, and nothing is deleted. The vault pauses for a moment while notes are saved or restored. Your keys are not in the backup. A backup holds notes and media only. Keep your key (or your signer) safe on its own; see Accounts & Keys in the app. On iPhone and Mac, start the vault before you export media. On iPhone and Android, the Vault tab has the same exports under Keep it full : Export notes and Back up media . Your follow list Following Backup A follow list on Nostr is one list that gets replaced every time it changes. A buggy app can wipe it. Nostr Vault keeps a snapshot each time your list changes, up to 50, on your device. Open Settings → Following Backup . Pick a snapshot. It shows who you no longer follow and who was added since. You can re-follow one person, or tap Restore This List to put the whole list back. Confirm. The restored list replaces your current one and is published to your relays. If your list was wiped somewhere else, Scan Relays looks for older copies of it on your relays. New in 3.0 Recently Deleted Posts you delete on a device stay in Settings → Recently Deleted on that device for 30 days. Un-delete posts it again as a new post. Likes and replies on the old post don't come back. Delete Forever removes the copy now. Profiles and lists aren't kept here. Recently Deleted is in the 3.0 apps and the web app; the apps you can download today are 2.7.2. In the browser Backups on the web The web app keeps its vault in your browser, so back it up if it holds anything you don't have elsewhere. Accounts → Backup : Export notes and Import notes make and read the same .zip as the phone apps, so either one restores the other. Photos and videos aren't in it. Settings → Backup & Restore : Download backup saves only the events you signed (notes, articles, profile, lists, likes) as a .jsonl file. Messages aren't in it. Choose a backup file reads that .jsonl back. Nothing is published either way. Notes Media Follow snapshots Recently Deleted iPhone .zip .zip Yes 3.0 Android .zip .zip Yes 3.0 Mac .zip .zip Yes 3.0 Web .zip or .jsonl No Yes Yes

d: Media servers (Blossom) in Nostr Vault: where photos go when you post, adding and removing servers, mirroring copies back to your device, the Media & Cache settings, and uploading from the share sheet.
h: What a media server is · Where a photo goes when you post · Add or remove a media server · Mirroring · Media & Cache · Uploading from the share sheet · Your device as a photo server
x: The basics What a media server is Relays only carry text. A photo or video is too big for that, so it goes to a media server instead, and your note holds a link to it. Nostr media servers speak a shared language called Blossom , so any Nostr app can read from them. A photo on a Blossom server is named by its fingerprint (a hash of the file). The same photo has the same name on every server, so it can be copied between servers and still be checked. Your account publishes a list of your media servers. Other apps read that list to find your files. When you post Where a photo goes when you post The app first saves the photo on this device, in your vault. It then uploads it to all of your outside media servers at once. As soon as one of them has it, the note is sent. The other servers keep uploading in the background. If no outside server takes the photo, the post is not lost. It waits under Settings → Media Servers in Waiting to send , and sends itself when a server answers. Tap Try sending now to retry straight away. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. A photo that is only on your phone can't be seen by anyone else, so the app won't post it without an outside server. Your list Add or remove a media server Open Settings → Media Servers . It sits in the Relays group, under Relays. Add: type the server's address (for example blossom.example.com ) in the box and tap the add button next to it. If you leave out https:// , the app adds it. Remove: tap the red button next to a server (a minus sign on iPhone and Mac, a bin on Android). Each change is saved and your updated list is published to your relays. If you set up Sync with Vault on Mac , your Mac is used as a media server too. It shows at the top of the page and you don't need to add it by hand. In the web app , the same page is Settings → Media Servers . Use Add and Remove , then Save and publish . Test checks that a saved server answers. The web app uploads to the server marked first first. If you have never published a list, it starts from two default servers. It also needs at least one server in the list. There is no button to reorder servers. In the web app, a server you add goes to the end of the list. Copies you own Mirroring Mirroring brings your own photos back from your media servers into your vault on this device, so they work offline and you keep a copy if a server goes away. Both controls are on the Media Servers page: Mirror Now downloads your media from your outside servers to this device, once. It shows progress while it runs. Auto-Mirror Media keeps doing it for you. Other people's photos Media & Cache When you look at photos and videos in the feed, the app keeps temporary copies so they load faster next time. You control this in Settings → Media & Cache , in the Feed & Display group. The web app doesn't have this page. Autoplay Videos plays videos as you scroll. Prefetch Profile Pictures loads profile pictures ahead of time for smoother scrolling. Disable Media Cache stops saving copies, so media downloads again each time. Keep Media For sets how long copies are kept: 1, 3, 7, 14 or 30 days, or Never. Clear Media Cache deletes the temporary copies to free space. Your vault and your media servers are not touched. On Android there is one more switch, Use Local Blossom Cache . It loads media through a Blossom cache app on the same phone, when one is running. Uploads never go through it. From other apps Uploading from the share sheet You can send photos and videos to Nostr Vault from your gallery or any other app, using the system share button. The two phones handle it differently: Phone What happens Android Pick Nostr Vault in the share sheet. The upload to Blossom starts straight away, one file at a time, with a notification while it runs. iPhone Pick Nostr Vault, then tap Add to Blossom upload queue . The files are added to a queue. Open Nostr Vault or tap its notification to finish the upload. On iPhone the upload happens in the app, not in the shar

d: How Nostr Vault share links work: Share and Copy Link make a nostrvault.app/thread/ link that opens the post in any browser as a guest, with a link preview card. Plus sharing photos into the app.
h: Share or copy a link · The link preview · Opening a link, with or without an account · Sharing photos into Nostr Vault
x: Sharing a post Share or copy a link Open the menu on any post. Share opens your phone's share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. On Android it's titled Share Note . Copy Link (Android and web: Copy link ) puts the link on your clipboard and shows Link copied . The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/thread/nevent1 . The nevent part names the post and its author, so the link works without any account and doesn't depend on one relay. Articles, videos and other posts have a Share button too, and give the same kind of link. In a chat or a feed The link preview When you paste the link in a chat app or a social site, it shows a preview card: the author's name (" on Nostr"), the start of the post, and the photo if the post has one. What they see Opening a link, with or without an account The link opens the post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. No account? They read the post and its replies as a guest. A bar at the top says Viewing as a guest , with Get the app and Sign in . They can open profiles and hashtags and come back to the post. Want to reply or like? Liking, replying, reposting and zapping need them to sign in. After signing in, the web app opens on the same post. Already signed in to the web app in that browser? The post opens in their account. A guest visit keeps nothing. Nothing is signed, and nothing is saved in the browser once the tab is closed. Photos load from their usual media server. If one can't be loaded there, the browser fetches it from the author's own device over the mesh. See The mesh . Deleted posts. If the author deletes the post, the link says This post was deleted by its author. Anyone who already saw it may still have a copy, as with anything you post publicly on Nostr. The other direction Sharing photos into Nostr Vault You can also send photos and videos from your Photos app or gallery to Nostr Vault, to upload them to your media server (Blossom). iPhone: pick up to 20 photos and 20 videos, tap Share, choose Nostr Vault, then Add to Blossom upload queue . Open Nostr Vault, or tap the Ready to upload to Blossom notification, to finish the upload. Android: share one or more photos or videos to Nostr Vault. The upload starts right away and shows Uploading to Blossom . Set up your account first. Uploading needs a public media server; see Settings → Relays → Media Servers .

d: Nostr Vault release notes for iPhone, Mac and Android: 3.0.0 (in testing) with the FIPS mesh, and the 2.7.2 builds you can download today.
x: Build 41 · iPhone, Mac and Android 3.0.0 In testing 3.0 is in testing and not released yet. The apps you can download today are 2.7.2. Nostr Vault 3.0 connects your own devices directly over the FIPS mesh , with no server in between. Your devices, connected. Turn on FIPS Mesh in Settings and add your devices by address or QR code. On Android you can add your Mac, your other phones or a home vault. See My Devices . iPhone and Mac: the mesh engine runs inside the Mac app, so there is nothing else to install. The Mac serves your photos to your own devices, and your public photos to anyone else who asks. See your own photo server . Notes and photos to your Mac. Add your Mac as Vault on Mac and each new note and photo goes to it over the mesh. Your notes and history also sync back from the Mac. iPhone and Mac: Check sync with Vault on Mac now ends on "Done" with counts, or says why it stopped. Home vault. A spare phone can be your home vault. It gets your new posts and media and passes them on. See kiosk mode . Photos over the mesh. Photos kept on your devices load over the mesh in the feed, the Vault and profiles. Your address stays private. Once you add a device, only your devices learn this phone's address. Anyone else gets public photos only. On Android, that is up to the limit you set under Pause after . See privacy . Android: if the mesh was on, it starts again with the relay when the phone restarts. Fixes iPhone: the phone ran hot with the app open. The relay now gets memory sized to the phone. iPhone and Mac: search no longer freezes while you type a common word. Android: on some phones the app ran out of memory and closed when a long note full of links was in the feed. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. Build 40 · iPhone, Mac and Android 2.7.2 (build 40) iPhone and Mac. This is the App Store build. The app now stays cool with it open all day. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays and signers. The Web of Trust globe draws more cheaply. On the iPhone, a locked article no longer links out to buy it on Fanfares. The Mac keeps that link. On both, it can only point at the article itself. New Message from a profile keeps the person you picked. Android. Android now looks and acts like the iPhone app. Messages and notifications, Settings, the tab bar, setup, profiles, search, follow lists, the Web of Trust globe, the feed, note details and the composer have all been matched to the iPhone. The app runs cooler. The relay pauses work nobody can see while the app is in the background, and backs off from flaky relays. A crash at launch on a new install is fixed. Build 39 · iPhone, Mac and Android 2.7.2 (build 39) iPhone and Mac. The App Store release candidate. Your keys and settings are safer. The config file is written in one go, backed up, and never reset by a damaged copy. Imported keys are checked. Fanfares articles get Open in Fanfares and Already unlocked? . The app itself never pays. Recipes, streams, articles and profiles can be opened in the rest of Nostr. Zaps on posts, live streams and articles are opt-in on the Mac, as on the iPhone. The on-chain wallet moves to Settings → Advanced . Highlights and comments from people you blocked no longer show under articles. iPad fixes for the relay card, the tour card and the Media viewer. Android. The App Store review pass for Android. Reposts, deletes, profile edits and follow-list changes are signed only as the account they belong to. Switching accounts can't carry one account's follow list into another. Settings are saved in one go and survive a damaged file. The owner key moves out of the config file, and a broken credential store no longer crashes the app. Notes backup works. Fanfares articles can be unlocked with a zap from the lock card. t: Build the mesh into your client
d: How another Nostr client can read photos over the FIPS mesh: the fipsmesh:// address form in kind 10063, plain Blossom GETs, and the NIP-F1 draft.
x: The mesh address is one new entry form, fipsmesh://<npub>/ , in lists you already use: the media server list ( kind:10063 ) and, later, the relay list ( kind:10002 ). No new event kinds. Requests are plain Blossom GET /<sha256> , with the same hash check. A client that doesn't know the form skips it and carries on with the other servers in the list. A client that does can ask the device for the photo by its fingerprint, the same way it asks any media server, and throws the photo away if the fingerprint doesn't match. Draft, not yet submitted NIP-F1: Nostr over the FIPS Mesh The address form, transport, safety rules for serving and reading, and where Nostr Vault implements each part. Read the draft → How it works for people using the app is on The mesh .
